extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students of literature, and writers studying D. H. Lawrence or modernist craft
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting the stylistic and thematic criteria visible in D. H. Lawrence's biography and criticism — the qualities, practices, and tendencies that define his prose and poetry (themes, tone, sensory focus, formal choices, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic focus: modernity, social alienation, industrialisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawrence's modernist works reflect on modernity, social alienation and industrialisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly presents Lawrence as a writer whose fiction and essays engage with the effects of industrial civilisation and the individual's separation from community and nature; works should be assessed by how they handle these concerns (e.g., The Rainbow's pre-industrial→industrial family arc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Championing sexuality, vitality and instinct
rubrics_metrics.description: His works 'champion sexuality, vitality and instinct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawrence foregrounds sexuality and physical vitality as central energies in his fiction and essays; evaluative attention goes to how candidly and philosophically sexual life and bodily instinct are represented, and whether those representations serve a wider moral/philosophical project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radical/explicit portrayal of romance and sexual language
rubrics_metrics.description: Four of his most famous novels ... were the subject of censorship trials for their radical portrayals of romance, sexuality, and use of explicit language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawrence deliberately used frank sexual depiction and strong/explicit diction (e.g., frequent use of 'fuck' and related words in Lady Chatterley's Lover). Assessment should note intentional provocation and whether explicitness contributes to literary intent rather than mere titillation; the page cites the later legal standard that 'literary merit' can justify explicit content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of characters to embody personal philosophy (philosophical fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Though often classed as a realist, Lawrence in fact uses his characters to give form to his personal philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how characters function as vehicles for ideas: are relationships and actions presented as explorations of Lawrence's philosophical positions (about sex, society, individuality) rather than mere social realism?

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on tactile/sensory detail — 'sense of touch'
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawrence was very interested in the sense of touch, and his focus on physical intimacy ... to restore an emphasis on the body and rebalance it with what he perceived to be Western civilisation's overemphasis on the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hallmark of Lawrence's craft is concentrated tactile imagery and attention to bodily sensation; assess writing for vivid physical detail, sensory immediacy, and how touch/physicality are used to shape character relationships and thematic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneity, personal sentiment, and anti-formulaic rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: "We can get rid of the stereotyped movements and the old hackneyed associations of sound or sense. ... We can break the stiff neck of habit.... But we cannot positively prescribe any motion, any rhythm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From his manifesto for later verse: value spontaneity and personal utterance; Lawrence's poetry aims to avoid hackneyed cadences and prescribed rhythms. Evaluate verse and prose for immediacy, freshness of movement, and avoidance of formulaic patterning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove artifice / aim for authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawrence rewrote some of his early poems ... to remove some of the artifice of his first works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawrence revised earlier work toward less artifice and more directness; assess drafts or poems for whether they have an authentic, unforced voice rather than ornate or contrived effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal, confessional inclination — 'lay himself bare'
rubrics_metrics.description: Look! We have come through! ... it reveals another important element common to much of his writings; his inclination to lay himself bare in his writings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawrence places value on exposing subjective feeling and disagreeable sensations; assess material for frank self-revelation and whether confessional honesty serves aesthetic and thematic ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic dialect and 'low-life' narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawrence's dialect poems reproduce the language and concerns of the people of Nottinghamshire ... Ezra Pound praised him for his 'low-life narrative'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of regional dialect and attention to working-class speech and concerns is a tool for verisimilitude and voice; evaluate whether dialect use is authentic, purposeful, and respectful of the material it represents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tackling grand themes and challenging conventional thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Both novels explore grand themes and ideas that challenged conventional thought on the arts, politics, economic growth, gender, sexual experience, friendship, and marriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawrence's major fiction engages large-scale social and philosophical questions; judging his work involves checking how effectively narrative and character interrogate or reframe conventional assumptions across these domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal experimentation: movement from Georgian forms to free verse and modernist techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been claimed that his early works clearly place him in the school of Georgian poets ... Later he wrote free verse influenced by Walt Whitman. 'We can get rid of the stereotyped movements...' (manifesto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawrence evolves in form: early conventional verse → freer, Whitman-influenced cadences and modernist experiments in prose and poetry. Evaluate formal risk-taking, changes in prosody, and adaptation of poetic line to subjectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of travel, landscape and natural world as formative material
rubrics_metrics.description: He often wrote about 'the country of my heart' as a setting for much of his fiction ... Lawrence is often considered one of the finest travel writers in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landscape and travel writings inform his fiction and essays; assess evocations of place, integration of local culture and settings, and how geography shapes character and theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with symbolism, mythic and religious material
rubrics_metrics.description: Works such as The Escaped Cock (reworking of the Resurrection story) and Apocalypse (a reflection on the Book of Revelation) show engagement with religious/mythic themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lawrence reinterprets myth and religious motifs; evaluate how symbolic or mythic elements are reworked (innovatively or problematically) and whether they deepen the work’s imaginative or philosophical scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy and dynamism versus complacency
rubrics_metrics.description: Later critics contrast Lawrence's energy and dynamism with the complacency of Georgian poetry; his best pages 'dance with life'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vitality of language and emotional intensity are recurring metrics for Lawrence's success; consider whether prose/poems convey kinetic force and life rather than static description.
